column2: Only three copies of the medieval manuscript are extant, all kept in European libraries.
column3: 這部中世紀手稿僅存三份，全都收藏在歐洲的圖書館。
column5: ex 外 + st 站（stand）：別人都倒了，只有它還站著留到現在

column2: Her extemporaneous toast, delivered without notes, moved the whole wedding party.
column3: 她不看稿的即席祝酒詞，感動了整場婚宴的賓客。
column5: ex 出 + tempor 時間（temporary 暫時）：當下就脫口而出
column7: ex - tem - po - ra - ne - ous

column2: Public health workers hoped to extirpate the disease from the region within a decade.
column3: 公共衛生人員希望在十年內把這種疾病從該地區根除。
column5: ex 出 + stirp 樹根：連根拔起，不留一點

column2: Her facetious remark about the broken printer made everyone laugh, though the boss was not amused.
column3: 她對壞掉印表機的玩笑話逗笑了大家，老闆卻笑不出來。
column4: facetious remark (不合時宜的玩笑話)
column5: facetious 依序含有 a e i o u 五個母音，像愛開玩笑的字謎

column2: Her felicitous phrase, "a library is a city of quiet," won warm applause.
column3: 她那句恰如其分的「圖書館是安靜的城市」贏得熱烈掌聲。
column5: felic 快樂（felicity 幸福）：用詞剛好，讓人舒服愉快

column2: The fervid crowd chanted the team's name until the stadium shook.
column3: 狂熱的群眾高喊球隊名字，直到整座球場都在震動。
column5: ferv 沸騰（fervent 熱切）：熱得像水煮開

column2: The senator launched a filibuster, reading cookbooks aloud for hours to delay the vote.
column3: 參議員發動冗長發言阻撓議事，連續數小時朗讀食譜以拖延表決。
column4: mount a filibuster (發動冗長阻撓)
column5: fill + buster：用長篇大論 fill 滿時間，把法案 bust 掉

column2: The fledgling company had only five employees but bold plans for expansion.
column3: 這家剛起步的公司只有五名員工，卻有大膽的擴張計畫。
column5: fledge 羽毛長齊 + ling 小東西：剛學飛的小鳥

column2: Drivers who flout the speed limit near schools risk heavy fines.
column3: 在學校附近無視速限的駕駛，有被重罰的風險。
column4: flout the law (公然違抗法律)
column5: 長得像 flaunt 炫耀：大搖大擺踩著規則走過去

column2: Rumors spread online can foment panic and unrest in a small town.
column3: 在網路上散布的謠言可能在小鎮煽動恐慌與動亂。
column5: 拉丁文 fomentum 是熱敷：不停加熱，火越燒越旺

column2: She forestalled complaints by sending customers a clear apology and a refund.
column3: 她寄給顧客明確的道歉與退款，預先阻止了抱怨。
column5: fore 前面 + stall 擋住：在前面先攔下來

column2: Her frugality showed in her habit of mending clothes instead of buying new ones.
column3: 她習慣縫補衣服而不買新的，顯示出她的節儉。
column5: frug 像 fruit 果實：珍惜每一顆果實，不浪費

column2: The editor fulminated against the new policy in a furious column.
column3: 編輯在一篇怒氣沖沖的專欄裡猛烈抨擊新政策。
column5: fulmin 是拉丁文閃電：怒罵像雷電劈下來

column2: Fulsome praise from the boss made the young analyst suspicious rather than flattered.
column3: 老闆過分諂媚的稱讚，讓年輕分析師起疑，而非受寵若驚。
column5: full 滿 + some：滿到過頭，膩得讓人不舒服

column2: No one could gainsay the evidence that the river had risen a full meter.
column3: 沒有人能否認河水已上升整整一公尺的證據。
column5: gain 是古英文「反對」+ say 說：開口說反話

column2: His rivals goaded him into answering the insult, which was exactly what they wanted.
column3: 對手激得他回應侮辱，這正是他們想要的。
column4: goad someone into (激得某人去做)
column5: 諧音「夠的」：牧人用尖棒一直戳，牛才會往前走

column2: Some shops gouge tourists by tripling prices once the festival begins.
column3: 有些商店在慶典一開始就把價格漲三倍，向觀光客敲竹槓。
column5: gouge 是鑿子：從荷包裡一鑿一大塊錢

column2: A gregarious host, she introduced every guest to at least three other people.
column3: 她是好交際的主人，把每位客人都介紹給至少三個人。
column5: greg 群體（congregate 聚集）：喜歡成群結隊

column2: Guileless and trusting, the boy believed every promise the salesman made.
column3: 天真又信任人的男孩，相信推銷員說的每一個承諾。
column5: guile 狡詐 + less 無：心裡沒有一點小心機

column2: The heterodox economist questioned assumptions that most of her colleagues had never examined.
column3: 這位非主流的經濟學家質疑多數同事從未檢驗過的假設。
column5: hetero 不同 + dox 意見（orthodox 正統）：意見與主流不同

column2: Critics called the fans' idolatry of the singer unhealthy, since they copied his every move.
column3: 評論者認為粉絲對這位歌手的盲目崇拜不健康，因為他們模仿他的一舉一動。
column4: idolatry of celebrities (對名人的盲目崇拜)
column5: idol 偶像 + latry 崇拜：把偶像當成神

column2: Loud noise over many years can impair hearing permanently.
column3: 長年的巨大噪音可能永久損害聽力。
column5: repair 是修理，im 的 impair 反過來：把功能弄壞

column2: He listened to the verdict with an impassive face, showing no sign of relief or fear.
column3: 他面無表情地聽完判決，沒有流露出鬆了口氣或恐懼。
column5: im 無 + pass 感受（passion 熱情）：臉上沒有任何感覺

column2: Imperturbable even in a storm, the pilot kept his voice calm while the plane shook.
column3: 即使在暴風雨中也從容不迫，飛行員在機身搖晃時聲音依然平穩。
column5: im 不 + perturb 擾亂 + able：怎麼擾都擾不亂

column2: Impetuous as ever, he quit his job on Monday and booked a flight on Tuesday.
column3: 他一如往常地衝動，週一辭職，週二就訂了機票。
column5: pet 衝撞（impetus 推動力）：沒多想就一頭衝出去

column2: The implacable critic refused every apology and kept attacking the company for years.
column3: 這位難以平息怒氣的批評者拒絕所有道歉，多年來不斷抨擊那家公司。
column5: im 不 + placate 安撫 + able：怎麼安撫都沒用

column2: The failing startup imploded within a year, torn apart by arguments among its founders.
column3: 這間營運不善的新創公司，在一年內因創辦人之間的爭執而內部崩潰。
column4: implode under pressure (在壓力下內部崩潰)
column5: im 向內 + plode 爆（explode 向外爆）：向內垮掉

column2: An inadvertent click deleted the file, and the whole team lost a day's work.
column3: 一次不經意的點擊刪掉了檔案，全組損失一天的工作。
column5: in 不 + advert 注意（advertise 引人注意）：沒注意到

column2: Compared with the main risk, the delay was inconsequential and not worth a meeting.
column3: 與主要風險相比，這次延誤微不足道，不值得開會討論。
column5: in 無 + consequence 後果：不會造成任何後果

column2: The indeterminate length of the project made it hard to hire contractors.
column3: 專案期限不確定，使得僱用外包人員很困難。
column5: in 不 + determine 決定 + ate：還沒決定下來

column2: Born into indigence, she worked her way through night school and became a surgeon.
column3: 她生於赤貧，靠半工半讀念夜校，後來成為外科醫師。
column5: indigent 窮的名詞版：連基本需要都缺

column2: Insensible to the cold after hours of climbing, he did not notice his frozen fingers.
column3: 爬了幾小時後對寒冷已沒有知覺，他沒發現自己的手指都凍僵了。
column5: in 無 + sense 感覺 + ible：沒有感覺，別和 insensitive 混淆

column2: The insipid soup needed salt, herbs, and a good deal of imagination.
column3: 那碗索然無味的湯需要鹽、香草，和不少想像力。
column5: in 無 + sip 啜飲：喝一口什麼味道都沒有

column2: The insularity of the small village meant that outside ideas rarely reached its council.
column3: 這個小村莊的偏狹閉塞，使外界的想法很少傳到村議會。
column5: insula 是拉丁文「島」（isolate 孤立）：像困在孤島上

column2: The union's intransigence over wages ended the talks after only one day.
column3: 工會在薪資問題上毫不讓步，談判只進行一天就破局。
column5: in 不 + trans 越過：一步也不肯跨過去讓步

column2: After the ad aired, the shop was inundated with orders it could not fill.
column3: 廣告播出後，這家店被大量無法應付的訂單淹沒。
column4: inundated with requests (被大量請求淹沒)
column5: 拉丁 unda 是波浪：一波接一波打來，把你淹掉

column2: Years of night shifts had inured the nurses to sleeping in daylight.
column3: 多年的夜班讓護理師習慣了在白天睡覺。
column5: 想像身體經過一次次磨練，皮變厚就不怕了

column2: He unleashed a stream of invective at the referee after the unfair call.
column3: 在不公平的判決之後，他對裁判劈頭痛罵了一長串。
column5: in 向 + vect 帶（vehicle 載具）：把惡言一車車載過去

column2: The itinerant storyteller traveled from village to village, trading tales for food and a bed.
column3: 巡迴的說書人穿梭於各村之間，以故事換取食物與床鋪。
column5: iter 路程（itinerary 行程表）：走過來走過去

column2: A heavy lassitude settled over the town during the humid August afternoons.
column3: 潮濕的八月午後，一股沉重的倦怠籠罩了全鎮。
column5: 諧音「懶西吐」：懶洋洋，連話都吐不出來
